_notes: Locally added -- upstream pinmame-nvram-maps has no X-Men map as of index rev 1406.
Records are 0x20 apart, NUL-terminated initials at +0x00, a 4-byte little-endian score at
+0x18, and a 16-bit checksum in the last two bytes of the first 30 -- the same record shape
the other Stern SAM maps use. The checksum verifies on all six records and fails on the
seventh, which is what bounds the block.
Confirmed against two cabinets: one still on Stern's factory ladder (75M/55M/40M/30M/25M
with 'G S'/'L R'/'J R'/'D T'/'P P'), the other with real play on it.
The sixth record is the Combo Champion, read off the machine's own champion display.
game on 24 (same platform), where a 4-byte stride reads player 2 as zero and player 3's
score as player 2's.
over from the verified 24 layout: no 3- or 4-player game has been played on either machine, and
In-progress scores are 4 bytes on 4-byte centres, verified by a 2-player game reading
3,119,500 and 4,467,600 at 0x021109E4 and 0x021109E8. Players 3 and 4 have not been observed:
no 3- or 4-player game has been played, and those bytes still sit inside a 0xFF fill the
firmware has never written.
player_count at 0x02110900 is verified on this ROM: it reads 1 after a 1-player game and 2 after
a 2-player one, and 24 uses the same address, so that field at least is shared across SAM games.
current_ball is at 0x00030AE5, in CPU RAM rather than NVRAM, identified by how it moves rather
than what it reads: across a whole game it stepped 1->2->3 and nothing else, with the score
climbing between the steps. Five exit snapshots had failed to find it, and the one other address
that survived those (0x0002FB20) turned out to cycle 0,1,2,5,4,3,2,1,4 -- a display value.
It is not the address 24 uses, which reads 16 here, nor does it mean anything on LUCI, which
reads 0. Like the score base and stride, the ball counter is per-ROM on SAM.
volume at 0x02110250 read 60 across four earlier captures and 40 after the operator set it to 40
on a 0-63 scale -- the only byte in the 128K that changed that way, so no second capture was
needed to confirm it.
current_player is the byte immediately below the ball, at 0x00030AE4. In a 4-player game it
completed 1->2->3 three times -- once per ball, as player-up rotating through four players does --
against one completion for the ball, and the two interlock: the ball stepped at the same scores
the player cycles finished at.
The four scores of that game read 721,760 / 1,099,300 / 853,880 / 1,302,140 exactly where this map
declares them, so the 4-byte stride is measured here rather than carried over from another ROM.
Only xmn_151h is claimed: the other X-Men revisions were not checked and SAM high score
addresses move between ROM revisions.
